title: Momentous decision looms after judges call for Netanyahu charges to be dropped
snippet:
Dropping of corruption charges against Israeli PM after unusual intervention could set damaging precedent

The Israeli judges presiding over Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial have called on prosecutors to end proceedings, a highly unusual intervention that leaves the attorney general facing a momentous political decision.

The prime minister has been charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three complex and overlapping criminal cases that hinge on his relationship with telecoms magnates and other wealthy businessmen. Ending the trial without a ruling could set damaging precedents for media independence and how politicians are held to account.

A UN tribunal has cast doubt on the evidence used to justify the sacking of Palestinian UN aid workers in 2024, saying it was based “almost entirely” on unproven assertions from the Israeli government and had damaged humanitarian operations in Gaza.

title: Tunisia NGO slams 'inhumane' prison conditions after dozens of detainee deaths
snippet:
Tunisia's main rights group on Friday denounced "inhumane" conditions in Tunisian prisons, saying 30 inmates have died since the beginning of summer, the country's hottest on record.

Authorities have yet to release figures for prison deaths after a summer marked by multiple heatwaves, water shortages and power cuts.

UNHCR's 2026 appeal targeted $8.5 billion -- of which only $2.9 billion has been raised to date.

title: War, fear drive Sudanese writer Baraka Sakin's fiction
snippet:
A lifetime of war and persecution has shaped the writing of Sudanese novelist Abdelaziz Baraka Sakin, who has turned the fear and longing that are so central to his experience into his main drive.

The 63-year-old fled Sudan for Europe in 2012 and then returned, dreaming of an end to his forced exile.

But the war that erupted in 2023 and killed more than 200,000 people pushed him out again.

Still, he keeps writing.
